model_comparison_summary.model_name: Champion: Monotonic WoE Logistic Scorecard (7 Features)
Challenger-Core: Monotone LightGBM (10 Features: Champion 7 w/ PAY_0_DPD + State Flags)
Challenger-Expanded: Monotone LightGBM (19 Features: Clean DPD Lags + State Flags)

production_recommendation_and_defence.production_recommendation: DEPLOY CHAMPION (7-Feature Monotonic WoE Logistic Scorecard) to Production; retain Monotone LightGBM (Challenger-Expanded) as Second-Line Benchmark / Shadow Challenger.
production_recommendation_and_defence.plain_assessment_of_performance_gap: The Challenger LightGBM is only marginally better in discrimination than the Champion Logistic Scorecard. On HOLDOUT (n=8,980), Challenger-Core improves AUROC by +0.0108 (from 0.7598 to 0.7706; Gini +0.0216 from 0.5197 to 0.5413), and Challenger-Expanded improves AUROC by +0.0132 (to 0.7730; Gini +0.0263 to 0.5460). In terms of probability accuracy on HOLDOUT, Brier score improves by 0.0035 (from 0.1402 on the Champion to 0.1369 raw / 0.1368 Platt-calibrated on Challenger-Expanded). A ~1.0% to 1.3% AUROC uplift does not justify replacing a transparent additive points scorecard with a 300-tree ensemble in production.

five_pillar_defence.1_performance_gap_and_shap_decomposition: Marginal uplift: HOLDOUT AUROC is 0.7598 (Champion) vs 0.7706 (Challenger-Core) and 0.7730 (Challenger-Expanded). In Challenger-Core, PAY_0_DPD and MONTHS_DELINQUENT_6M account for 42.47% of total |SHAP| magnitude, while repayment capacity (MEAN_PAY_AMT_6M), utilisation (MEAN_UTIL_RATIO_6M), revolving frequency (MONTHS_REVOLVING_6M), balance trend (BILL_TREND_6M_RATIO), credit limit (LIMIT_BAL), and Month-1 non-delinquent state indicators account for the remaining 57.53%. In Challenger-Expanded, all 8 DPD arrears variables combined account for 41.59% of total |SHAP|.
five_pillar_defence.2_explainability_and_gdpr_article_22: Under EU GDPR Article 22 (automated individual decision-making, including profiling), data subjects have the right to obtain meaningful information about the logic involved in automated credit decisions. The Champion Scorecard provides an exact, deterministic additive points schedule (32 bins across 7 features) where the logic and point contribution of each variable can be stated directly to the customer and credit committee. By contrast, LightGBM relies on post-hoc TreeSHAP decompositions across 300 depth-5 trees, where a feature's marginal log-odds impact varies with higher-order tree splits.
five_pillar_defence.3_monotonicity_and_non_delinquent_codes: Raw PAY_x codes (-2 inactive, -1 paid duly, 0 revolving) are non-monotonic in empirical default rates (e.g., on DEV, PAY_0 bad rates are 12.88% at -2, 16.49% at -1, and 12.67% at 0; PAY_2 bad rates are 17.95% at -2, 15.88% at -1, and 15.79% at 0). In the Challenger, monotonicity is properly enforced by applying +1 constraints strictly to PAY_x_DPD = max(PAY_x, 0) while leaving the binary state indicators (-2, -1, 0) unconstrained. In the Champion, coarse WoE binning (-2 vs {-1, 0} vs 1 vs 2+) achieves strict monotonicity across its 4 intervals, but at the cost of a known limitation recorded in the Challenge Log: PAY_0 Bin 2 merges -1 (16.49% DEV default rate) with 0 (12.67% DEV default rate), which are different risks.
five_pillar_defence.4_stability_and_overfitting_control: The Champion estimates 8 parameters (intercept + 7 slopes) on 32 coarse bins, showing a DEV-to-HOLDOUT AUROC drop of 0.0163 (0.7761 -> 0.7598). Challenger-Expanded fits 300 trees (up to 31 leaves each) and shows a larger full-DEV-to-HOLDOUT AUROC drop of 0.0259 (0.7989 -> 0.7730).
five_pillar_defence.5_regulatory_auditability_irb: Under CRR Articles 174-180 and EBA Guidelines on PD/LGD estimation (EBA/GL/2017/16), retail IRB rating systems must demonstrate clear risk differentiation across grades, transparent parameterisation, and independent Second-Line (2LoD) replicability and challenge. The Champion Scorecard is trivial to audit, validate, and govern, while Challenger-Expanded serves as the Second-Line benchmark model to monitor potential non-linear interaction drift. Governance Trigger: a HOLDOUT Gini gap of 5 points (0.0500) or more between Challenger and Champion triggers a formal Champion review.

governance_trigger_threshold.metric: HOLDOUT Gini Gap (Challenger Gini minus Champion Gini)
governance_trigger_threshold.action_if_breached: Formal Second-Line (2LoD) Champion Review and Scorecard Redevelopment / Recalibration.

production_recommendation_and_defence.known_champion_limitation_for_challenge_: PAY_0 Bin 2 merges -1 (16.49% DEV default rate, n=3,965) with 0 (12.67% DEV default rate, n=10,294), which are different risks (+3.82 percentage points higher default rate on -1 than 0). Because numeric PAY_0 orders -2, -1, 0 sequentially, monotonic interval binning on raw PAY_0 cannot separate -1 from 0 without violating monotonicity against -2 (12.88% DEV default rate). By contrast, the Challenger decomposes PAY_0 into PAY_0_DPD = max(PAY_0, 0) plus separate unconstrained state indicators (PAY_0_IS_PAID_DULY, PAY_0_IS_REVOLVING, PAY_0_IS_INACTIVE).
